step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram shows an event-driven data lake ingestion and processing pipeline at Zalando. First, external microservices send events into Nakadi (a custom event bus represented as a ThirdParty component). Nakadi batches these events and writes them into an S3 Archival Bucket. Object creation events trigger an SQS Queue, which invokes a Lambda function to partition and write data into an S3 RAW Bucket. From the S3 RAW Bucket, object creation triggers another SQS Queue and Lambda function that enriches message attributes and pushes them to an SNS Topic. The SNS Topic fans out to multiple SQS Queues filtered by event type for downstream processing (e.g. Spark jobs), as well as to a reformatting pipeline consisting of Lambda, an SQS Queue, and an S3 MAIN Bucket for ad-hoc querying.
